newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian miner WMC seeks international expansion.
newsitem.headline: Australian miner WMC seeks international expansion.

text.p: Mining house WMC Ltd may call Australia home, but increasingly it wants to make a bigger splash internationally and has several major resource projects pending worldwide, managing director Hugh Morgan said on Friday.
Australia's third largest miner has mapped out a growth plan that extends from the Philippines to Cuba to Uzbekistan.
Contributions from Australian operations underpinned a 20.4 percent rise in WMC's net profit to A$386 million (US$305 million) for the year to June 30, 1996, it reported this week.

Morgan told Reuters in an interview that Australia still offers opportunities for mining companies but is no longer as attractive as it once was. Australians have a "love-hate" relationship with miners, he said.

An arsenal of government regulations and aboriginal land rights issues have fostered much uncertainty in the Australian mining sector and is encouraging some companies to go elsewhere to expand, Morgan said.
Mining in Australia is "a lot harder than it used to be, and others (countries) have got a lot more accommodating," he said.
In Uzbekistan, WMC wants to establish a joint venture to exploit the Zarmitan gold deposit, possibly the richest in the world.
"Uzbekistan geologically is a very attractive place to be," Morgan said.
Morgan also sees opportunities in the Philippines, where it is prospecting for copper and gold on Mindanao Island.
In Cuba, the company is searching for nickel, risking the wrath of the United States, which has long-imposed trade sanctions on the island nation.
"If we're going to go where the major ore bodies are, we are going to have to accept higher risk," Morgan said.
Morgan said strong competition exists among resource-rich countries to attract investment in mining.
Mining companies seeking foreign investments should look more to the future than the present when assessing political and economic risks, he said.
"Present assessment is not the be all and end all, because this is a business where you have 10- to 20-year lead times. It's really important to understand where a country is headed," he said.
Still, despite a desire to expand internationally, WMC is spending heavily to ensure a long-term presence at home.
The company has earmarked A$1.25 billion to double copper production at the Australian Olympic Dam deposit, the single largest investment by WMC in its 63-year history.
